clue.text: Al Reid's busy before 1 PM

indicators.note: busy suggests the letters of Al Reid's bustling about into a new order

parts.note: the numeral one is written as the Roman I

explanation.surface: Someone called Al Reid has a hectic morning before one o'clock in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like a time of day beside '1', but it is the definition: Prime Minister. 'busy' rearranges AL REIDS into DISRAEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was twice Prime Minister of Britain under Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Made a claim from government department

parts.note: the state is the governing body of a country
D is a short abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: Someone lodged a claim with, or drawn from, a government department.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made a claim is to have asserted or declared something, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Delightful group of goldfinches perched on bank

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece perched on another sits above it

parts.note: a charm is the collective noun for goldfinches
ING is a Dutch banking group

explanation.surface: A lovely flock of goldfinches sits on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a riverbank in the picture, but it is ING, the Dutch bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and delightful are synonyms for something pleasing and attractive.

clue.text: Finished parts function horizontally

definitions.note: an adverb, while the answer is an adjective meaning lying flat on one's back

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the function's letters are separated to take in the other piece

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
up means finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: Completed sections perform their role lying flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' is a verb: SINE parts to let UP in. 'function' looks like a verb but is the trigonometric noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying face upward means lying flat, so the position is horizontal.

clue.text: Riddle cracked by Welsh writer

indicators.note: cracked by says the first word is broken open to admit the second

parts.note: to riddle is to sieve, or sift

explanation.surface: A puzzle is solved by an author from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle being cracked, but it is the sieve sense: SIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was the Irish satirist who wrote Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Theatre is regularly breaking Aussie state law

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the picked letters split the state abbreviation

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Australia

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words Theatre is

explanation.surface: Drama is routinely flouting the law of an Australian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of THEATRE IS, which go inside SA, South Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharia is Islamic religious law, derived from the Koran and the prophet's teachings.

clue.text: Urgency having previously contracted the fungal disease

indicators.note: having previously says the shortened word goes before the urgency piece
contracted means shortened, so the last letter of the is dropped

parts.note: the word the, shortened
a rush is a state of urgency

explanation.surface: In a hurry, someone has caught a fungal infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' reads as catching the disease, but it shortens THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrush is the common name for candidiasis, a yeast infection.

clue.text: Beginning with Hastings, a king of the past

definitions.text: Beginning with Hastings, a king of the past

indicators.note: beginning with picks the opening letter of Hastings

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
old means belonging to former times

explanation.surface: A monarch of history, whose story begins with Hastings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the last Anglo-Saxon king died at the Battle of Hastings in 1066, and his story is often begun there.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Godwinson was the English king killed at Hastings in 1066.

clue.text: Some mushrooms to munch before nosing around

parts.note: to champ is to chew noisily, to munch

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of nosing are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal chews before sniffing about, perhaps a pig after truffles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal here, not a placement word.
explanation.definitionFit: Champignons are field or button mushrooms, from the French word for mushroom.

clue.text: Some hosts argue with women going ape

indicators.note: hosts means holds inside, so the first piece takes in the second

parts.note: part means some of something

indicators.note: going says the letter for women leaves the word for argue

parts.note: to row is to argue

explanation.surface: Some party hosts quarrel while the women lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ape' is a verb here, to mimic, not the animal. 'going' removes the women, and 'hosts' holds one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape is to mimic, and to parrot is to repeat or imitate mindlessly.

clue.text: Clothing arrives here in German jet

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping around, so the German word dresses the abbreviation

parts.note: hier is German for here
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: Clothing turns up here aboard a German aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German jet' looks like one phrase, but 'German' belongs with 'here'. The Harrier is a British jump jet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Harrier is a British vertical take-off military jet aircraft.

clue.text: Appeal to stop Grand Duke's last dud cheque

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the appeal piece fills the space between the others

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, and a grand is a thousand pounds

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of Duke

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A plea to a Grand Duke to stop a worthless cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand Duke' looks like a title, but 'Grand' gives K and 'Duke's last' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiting is writing cheques without funds, so a kite is a slang term for a worthless cheque.

clue.text: After rally, Leslie bumped into girl

parts.note: a demo is a protest rally

indicators.note: bumped into suggests the letters of Leslie are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: After a protest march, a man called Leslie ran into a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumped into' looks like a meeting, but it rearranges LESLIE into ISELLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoiselle is a literary or French-derived word for a young unmarried woman.

clue.text: Victorian statistician in the dark, during storm

parts.note: the dark hours are night
in means during, as in 'in the morning'
a gale is a storm wind

explanation.surface: A Victorian numbers expert caught out in darkness during a tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence Nightingale is famed as a nurse, but she was also a pioneering statistician, known for her polar-area diagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence Nightingale used statistical charts to argue for hospital reform in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Harry had wingless duck and hen with fleshy hindquarter

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the letters are worried into a new order
wingless removes the outer letters of duck, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: Harry ate a duck and a hen, minus wings, with meaty haunches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the anagram signal on HAD, UC and HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The haunch is the hip and thigh, so a creature so described has fleshy hindquarters.

clue.text: Blooming fellow leaving with a menacing scowl …

indicators.note: leaving says the fellow's letter goes out of the blooming word

parts.note: blooming means flowering

explanation.surface: A fellow in full bloom walks off scowling darkly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' could be a mild British expletive, but it means FLOWERING here.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour or lower is to frown or look threatening, so a lowering look is a menacing scowl.

clue.text: … interviews very old man about old times

definitions.note: plural noun, while the answer names a kind of street interview collectively

indicators.note: about here means next to, so the father piece stands alongside the others

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
pop is a familiar word for one's father, the old man

explanation.surface: Street interviews with a very elderly man about times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: Vox pop, short for Latin vox populi, is a British term for street interviews of the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Vox pops are brief interviews with passers-by, gathering public opinion for broadcasts.

clue.text: Enjoy a dip

definitions.meaning: to enjoy something is to savour it with pleasure
a dip is a sauce or pickle eaten with food, a condiment

explanation.surface: Have fun taking a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to take pleasure in, and the noun is a tangy sauce or dip.

clue.text: Our Darren goes out around noon for a quick one

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the noon letter
goes out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A man called Darren pops out at lunchtime for a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quick one' suggests a quick drink; it is a fast bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is an American ground cuckoo famed for running at great speed.

clue.text: Lecturer welcomes old German scientist

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the lecturer word surrounds the German one

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
alt is German for old

explanation.surface: A university teacher greets an aged German researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German scientist' looks like one phrase; 'German' belongs with 'old'. Dalton was English.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dalton was the English chemist who developed atomic theory.

clue.text: Single female recruited by foreign army branch

indicators.note: recruited by says the other letters are taken into the rearranged army
foreign suggests the letters of army are made strange, rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A lone woman joins a foreign army's division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges ARMY into RAMY, which takes in IF.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramify is to spread out into branches, so it means to branch, as a verb.

clue.text: London designer tucked into dinner with revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
tucked into says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A London designer eats heartily at a dinner with a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'tucked into' in the definition, but it is the hiding signal: the definition is only 'London designer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren was the architect of St Paul's Cathedral and many London churches.

clue.text: Lost place in book

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has lost their place in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Pelican was Penguin's imprint of non-fiction paperbacks, so a Pelican is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelican Books is a non-fiction paperback imprint, so one such title is a book.

clue.text: Member of Rat Pack is out of cocktails (unlikely as it seems!)

indicators.note: out of says the little word leaves the cocktails

parts.note: martinis are gin-and-vermouth cocktails

explanation.surface: A Rat Pack crooner has run out of cocktails, which seems improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket jokes that a Rat Pack singer would never run dry of martinis.
explanation.definitionFit: Dean Martin sang with Frank Sinatra and Sammy Davis Jr in the Rat Pack.

clue.text: It's billed with nothing about price? Just the reverse

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
just the reverse says the roles flip, so the price goes round nothing instead

parts.note: love means nil, nothing, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Something advertised with nothing said about its cost, or perhaps the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'billed' looks like charged on a bill, but means having a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A plover is a wading bird, and anything with a beak can be called billed.

clue.text: Actor who won posthumous award has following in Switzerland

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A dead film star's award has fans in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Finch won the Best Actor Oscar for Network after his death in 1977.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Finch was the first actor to win an Academy Award after dying.
